module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 280

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/280](https://www.erdosproblems.com/280)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial
  number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos280

open Filter

/-- The integer `m` is covered by one of the first `k` chosen congruence classes. -/
def isCoveredBy (n a : ℕ → ℕ) (m k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, m % n i = a i

/-- The number of integers below `n k` not covered by the first `k` congruence classes. -/
noncomputable def uncoveredCount (n a : ℕ → ℕ) (k : ℕ) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact ((Finset.range (n k)).filter (fun m => ¬ isCoveredBy n a m k)).card

/--
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots $ be an infinite sequence of integers with associated $a_k\pmod{n_k}$, such that for some $\epsilon>0$ we have $n_k>(1+\epsilon)k\log k$ for all $k$. Then
$$
\#\{ m<n_k : m\not\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i} \textrm{ for }1\leq i\leq k\}\neq o(k).
$$

Cambie observed that this is false.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos280.lean"]
theorem erdos_280 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (n a : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 1 ≤ i → a i < n i) →
      (∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧
        ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → (n k : ℝ) > (1 + ε) * (k : ℝ) * Real.log (k : ℝ)) →
      ¬ Tendsto
        (fun k : ℕ => (uncoveredCount n a k : ℝ) / (k : ℝ))
        atTop (nhds 0) := by
  sorry

end Erdos280

reformulations.difference: The helper tests `m % n i = a i`, while the source uses congruence classes with arbitrary representatives. The main theorem restricts representatives to `a i < n i` for positive indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the theorem's representative bounds, `a i % n i = a i`, so the helper is equivalent to existence of an index 1 ≤ i ≤ k with `Nat.ModEq (n i) m (a i)`. This equivalence was proved in scratch. All used moduli are positive, and every congruence class has a canonical representative satisfying the bounds. In particular, the source's counterexample has a₁ = 2 modulo 2, represented in Lean by a₁ = 0.

reformulations.difference: The source says the uncovered count is not `o(k)`; Lean negates convergence of its real-valued quotient by k to zero, using a sequence indexed by all natural numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since k is eventually nonzero at `atTop`, Mathlib's `Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff_tendsto'` proves that the count is `o(k)` exactly when this quotient tends to zero. Negating preserves the equivalence. The division-by-zero convention at k = 0 is irrelevant. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/280 (complete formulas and remarks, read via https://r.jina.ai/http://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/280)
Erdős and Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), Chapter 3, especially p. 29: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf
review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The source's negative answer agrees with `answer(False)` and `research solved`. The exact linked Lean proof compiled successfully; /workspace/review/proof-bridge.lean also derives the repository's exact statement from it, with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Boundary checks establish positivity of every used modulus, harmlessness of the dummy zero index, and invariance of the limit if zero is excluded from the count. Computable equivalents of the helpers reproduce Cambie's constant uncovered count through k = 10. The reviewed file was not modified.
